The ordinary and adaptive metrics have the exact mixed parameter a alpha. A two-term inverse cancels its first correction, giving the full a-cubed forcing error. Arbitrarily small unknown-error coefficients undo the fixed cutoff-collar rescaling.

All three adaptive regions are retained. The bounded region uses the complete global estimate with full column errors; both sign regions use the symmetric imaginary-part identity, signed time weights and the entire double commutator.

A uniformly controlled canonical chart retains the real factor exactly. Its section, hitting inverse, Hamilton flow, symplectic pullback and derivative bounds are explicit. The real factor need not vanish at the marked point.

The existing actual complex barriers provide the three strict real-part margins. A fixed finite cover in normalized variables gives uniform cutoffs and transported exponents, proving every part of Lemma 26.10.5.

Complex powers retain every logarithmic derivative, time support and the first time derivative. Time mollification extends the earlier estimates to the actual C1-in-time vectors without differentiating the coefficients.

The exact time commutator and transverse bracket cancel the transported part. All outgoing and lower-order errors are bounded at order a; retained derivative energy absorbs the remaining square-root-a logarithmic coefficient.

Weighted reconstruction and ordinary/adaptive transfer use full finite product remainders, including countably many centers as one Hilbert-valued column. Actual final absorption gives the complete localized estimate.

Whole homogeneous graph reduction and elliptic order reduction preserve the unknown index and give precisely the m-minus-one source shift. Full temporal lower-term removal and the all-frequency gauge retain the complete operator.

The geometric width is fixed before its frequency threshold. A full left-quantized shell test has actual compact time support, weak norm lambda to minus one quarter and full forcing norm lambda to minus five quarters.

The measured composition contains the complete spacetime bracket, including the temporal-frequency derivative. Endpoint regular collars and the elliptic complementary support control its actual leading measurement.

Tangential auxiliary symbols are not treated as uniform ordinary full-frequency symbols on the temporal axis. The time derivative is split exactly; complete normalized-shell and tangential products, arbitrarily deep finite remainders and actual negative Sobolev input control every tail.
The shell limit gives index sigma minus three epsilon halves; its all-epsilon limit and a finite quarter bootstrap give the full target index without asserting endpoint Sobolev membership.

All characteristic strata are covered. Rank-one arcs in the rank-two saturation have the zero quadratic jet by their nonnegative factorization. Escaping arcs use the favorable incoming endpoint. Residual arcs use the full localized proof.

For the nonzero-quadratic extension, actual cutoff localization and artificial time retraction add matching quadratic endpoints without additional source data. The genuine full-variable classical operator is specified on the working conic tube. Indefinite descent or corrected semidefinite propagation is used only with a constant comparison.

Radial curves use conic index constancy. A repeated projected orbit is an embedded circle; cutting in a known good arc proves the compact theorem on its complement. Global quasi-concavity is not inferred from local quasi-concavity.

The compact theorem yields every finite constant comparison, then the full extended-valued quasi-concavity theorem on open, closed or half-open intervals and at every real operator order. This completes receiving Section 26.10.

Three complete solutions verify the exact complex barrier, two-term inverse cancellation and every quarter-bootstrap shell power. Thirty-five exact checks, 352 formulas, 44 numbered displays and eighteen inspected lesson captures support the proof review.

component_scope: A global solution estimate measures the entire forcing. Propagation needs a forcing measurement in a smaller phase-space region. Complex transported weights supply that localization: their real parts are small where regularity is wanted and large where a cutoff changes. We prove the complete localized estimate, then use frequency shells to recover the Sobolev index on every one-dimensional characteristic interval.
